summary: Frontend-only verification of the fully rewritten /xoiris-scheduling (Iris.jsx). Validated hero, all 9 sections, 4 plain (non-collapsible) numbered feature lists, new 'Working with Your EHR' section, 10-item spec table with 0px border-radius, 6-question FAQ accordion expand/collapse, In-the-system link, DemoCTA, no em/en dashes in rendered copy, 1920px + 390px viewports, light + dark theme, and cold-load navbar dropdown navigation. All 14 requested items PASS. Zero console/page errors, zero horizontal overflow on mobile. Backend testing skipped as instructed (static page).

issues: The IMAGES.abstract hero visual renders extremely low-contrast/near-invisible against the light background - it reads as empty whitespace on the right half of the hero. Cosmetic only, not a functional defect.

critical_code_review_comments: Iris.jsx is 419 lines and self-contained; the local FeatureList component is duplicated in spirit across product pages (System.jsx etc). Consider extracting to /components/common/FeatureList.jsx to avoid future drift.
FeatureList rows have no data-testid; tests had to rely on structural class selectors (span.font-mono.text-[11px]). Adding data-testid="feature-list-item" would harden future automation.
Section locators for 'Patient Communication' collide with hero subhead copy containing the same phrase; not a bug, just noted for test authors.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iris.jsx verified fully at iteration 31. Verified counts: Filling the Day = 7 items, Patient Communication = 6, Intake and Records = 4, Security and Access = 5, all rendered as plain divide-y lists with 0 button/[data-state] elements inside those sections (confirmed non-collapsible). Specs table = 10 rows, computed border-radius 0px, includes both new items. FAQ = 6 Radix triggers, data-state closed->open->closed verified. 3 x /request-a-demo links on page, journey link href=/xo-vision-care-system. NOTE: eyebrows use CSS text-transform:uppercase, so inner_text() returns them uppercased - compare case-insensitively or tests will false-fail. Also note the display font renders capital I in 'xoIris' like a lowercase l - not a text bug. The reported one-time navbar-dropdown non-navigation glitch could NOT be reproduced on a cold home-page load + immediate hover/click (navigated correctly).
rca_of_the_issue: No defects found. The only initially-reported failures in my first run were test-harness artifacts: (1) uppercase text-transform on eyebrows, and (2) a section locator matching the hero because the hero subhead contains the phrase 'patient communication'. Both corrected in the second run and everything passed.
